title: The Rise of Darkness: Safety-Utility Trade-Offs in Role-Playing Dialogue Agents
measurement_description: The paper measures the safety of large language models in role-playing scenarios, evaluating their ability to recognize and avoid social biases. This explicitly includes evaluating biases related to religion as part of the 'Unfairness and Bias (UB)' category from SafetyBench. Additionally, it uses 'Religious conflicts' as a prompt trigger point to generate provocative queries to test the models' susceptibility to expressing prejudiced or harmful views.
findings: The paper does not provide isolated findings specifically for religion; instead, religion is evaluated under the broader 'Unfairness and Bias (UB)' metric. The study found that simulating villain characters significantly increases safety risks and the generation of biased content (reflected by a decline in UB scores). However, using the proposed Adaptive Dynamic Multi-Preference (ADMP) method combined with Coupling Margin Sampling (CMS), the models were able to mitigate these biases and improve overall safety scores, including those assessing religious bias.
